tools.name: dedot_login

tools.name: dedot_logout

tools.name: dedot_status
tools.description: Check Dedot connection status and view your current profile. Also flushes any pending events (NEW_CANDIDATES, MATCH_FOUND, MATCH_CONFIRMED) that arrived while offline.

tools.name: dedot_register_profile
tools.description:
Register a professional profile on Dedot after the user has reviewed and approved it. FIELD MEANING (read carefully): `can_help_with` = what the user is **SELLING** (skills/outcomes they deliver). `looking_for` = what the user is **BUYING** (people they need, services they want, or problems they have). `personal_interests` = **hobbies and fun**, not work topics. SAMPLES are embedded in the tool input schema for each array field — follow that level of specificity. IMPORTANT: Do NOT call this tool directly. First: (1) gather context from ALL available sources — local files (memory.md, CLAUDE.md, tasks.md) AND your built-in memory system AND this conversation AND any project context in this session — use whatever is available; do NOT say "no local files" if you have context from memory or conversation, (2) show the complete draft to the user for review and editing, (3) wait for explicit approval — "looks good", "send it", "yes". Only call this tool after the user approves. PROFILE QUALITY RULES — apply before submitting: Every looking_for item must read like something you are trying to **buy or get help with** — WHO needs to show up and WHAT problem (not "collaborators" — say "founders who need help turning LinkedIn content into qualified pipeline without spammy automation"). Every can_help_with item must read like something you **sell or deliver** — SPECIFIC SKILL and OUTCOME (not "content strategy" — say "LinkedIn content strategy that converts profile views into booked calls for technical founders"). Never submit generic phrases: "networking", "collaborators", "like-minded people", "general advice", "business growth", "opportunities", "partnerships", "connections", "synergies". Specificity test: if a phrase would match 80% of professionals, rewrite it. If context is too thin, ask the user using the field definitions above — not generic career questions. Raw context is never sent — only the user-approved structured summary. If the user signed up via a referral link, pass referred_by_code (the short code from dedot.ai/join/{code}). FULL WORKED EXAMPLE (shape + teaching; omit Mongo-only fields like _id, userId, embeddingVector):

{
  "name": "James Hart",
  "one_line_bio": "Former product marketing lead; now focused on helping technical founders find their first hundred happy users.",
  "what_i_do": "Head of Growth at a B2B SaaS; I design GTM experiments, partner programs, and early-adopter onboarding for developer-facing products. Currently launching a playbook for PLG plus founder outreach for devtools startups in APAC.",
  "can_help_with": [
    "Go-to-market experiment design including channel testing positioning and onboarding flows for developer-facing B2B SaaS products from first users through repeatable early traction in APAC markets",
    "Founder-led sales coaching pipeline design and messaging workshops for teams shipping technical products without a classic enterprise sales bench or full AE coverage yet"
  ],
  "looking_for": [
    "AI-native product teams that want a part-time GTM advisor to sharpen positioning launch sequencing and beta narrative before a wide release or fundraising conversation with serious technical buyers",
    "Technical founders building MCP or agent-first tooling who want structured design partners for closed beta interviews feedback loops and repeatable founder-led sales experiments in their vertical"
  ],
  "company": "RiseStack Analytics",
  "industry": "B2B SaaS",
  "location": "Hanoi, Vietnam",
  "personal_interests": [
    "Weekend trail runs around West Lake plus slow breakfast meetups with local operators after a long week on the keyboard",
    "Casual street photography walks through the historic Old Quarter in Hanoi and occasionally printing small zines for friends instead of posting everything online"
  ],
  "open_to": [
    "Advisory conversations",
    "Beta testing new networking or agent products",
    "Warm intros to GTM operators"
  ]
}

NOTE: Older docs or legacy DB rows may show short chip labels (e.g. "Go-to-market strategy"); the live API requires each can_help_with and looking_for item to be 8+ descriptive words.

personal_interests must be hobbies and fun — never work stack keywords like "AI agents" or "B2B SaaS".

name.description: Full legal or display name as shown on the profile.

one_line_bio.description: One-line tagline (aim ≤12 words). Example: "Building AI-native tools for professional networking."

what_i_do.description: What you do day-to-day AND what you are actively shipping or building (2–3 sentences). This is identity + current work in one field.

can_help_with.description: What you are SELLING — concrete skills or outcomes you deliver for others (each item must be 8+ words on the server). SAMPLE: "Scaling Node.js and TypeScript APIs on AWS for early-stage B2B SaaS teams from MVP to production traffic." SAMPLE: "LinkedIn positioning and content strategy for technical founders who want inbound leads without spammy automation." NOT: "networking", "general advice", "strategic partnerships".

looking_for.description: What you are BUYING — people you need, services you want, or problems you need help with (each item 8+ words on the server). SAMPLE: "Senior backend engineers who have shipped production MCP servers and can harden our OAuth and connector security model." SAMPLE: "Founders or GTM leads who want to turn conference talks and long-form posts into a repeatable outbound pipeline." NOT: "collaborators", "new opportunities", "like-minded people".

company.description: Current company or organisation (empty string if independent).

location.description: City + country, e.g. "Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam", "London, UK".

personal_interests.description: HOBBIES and things you do for fun — explicitly NOT your work stack or learning topics. SAMPLE: "Sunday road cycling and cafe rides with a local club." SAMPLE: "Film photography and darkroom printing on weekends." SAMPLE: "Chess and online puzzle games after work."

open_to.description: Kinds of relationships you are open to, e.g. "clients", "co-founders", "advisors", "contractors", "investors", "hiring".

callbackUrl.description: Optional HTTP URL where Dedot will POST events (NEW_CANDIDATES, MATCH_FOUND, MATCH_CONFIRMED)

referred_by_code.description: Optional code from dedot.ai/join/{code} — records attribution for leaderboard (no billing while pre-pricing).

tools.name: dedot_deregister
tools.description: Remove your profile from the Dedot network. You will no longer appear in matches. This cannot be undone.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm profile deletion

tools.name: dedot_get_candidates
tools.description: Fetch your candidate shortlist — people Dedot thinks you should meet. By default re-runs vector search + structured rules on the server so results reflect other users' latest profiles and embeddings (not just a stale cache). Set refresh=false only to read the last saved shortlist without an Atlas round-trip. Optionally pass a free-text `query` (e.g. "anyone working on AI for financial advisors?") to search the network by topic instead of by profile similarity — the server embeds the query and searches with it. When query is set, refresh is ignored. Returns anonymised profiles with match data. When presenting candidates, generate a two-way fit explanation for each one. Compare the user's looking_for (what they are buying) against the candidate's can_help_with (what they sell), and vice versa. For each candidate explain: (1) what the user gets from this connection, (2) what the candidate gets, (3) one conversation starter based on shared context. Use plain language, be specific about which fields overlap, and keep it to 2-3 sentences. If the fit is weak or one-sided, say so honestly. Then ask if they want to evaluate them, and use `dedot_evaluate`.

refresh.description: If true (default), recompute shortlist via vector search + rules. If false, return cached shortlist only. Ignored when query is set.

query.description: Optional free-text search query (max 500 chars). When provided, embeds this text and searches the network by topic instead of by profile similarity. Use when the user asks an ad-hoc question like "anyone working on AI for financial advisors?" or "who can help with React development?".

tools.name: dedot_evaluate
tools.description: Submit evaluation results for one or more candidates. IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, evaluate each candidate using ALL available context — not just the anonymised profile card. Use local files (memory.md, CLAUDE.md, tasks.md), your built-in memory system, and this conversation to understand what the user actually needs. For each candidate: reason about fit using every source of context you have, state your recommendation and why, then ask the user "Shall I submit these evaluations?" and wait for approval before calling this tool. interested=true signals mutual interest; if both sides say yes, a mutual match is created.

candidateProfileId.description: The candidate profile ID from the shortlist

interested.description: true = interested in connecting, false = not interested

reason.description: Optional reason — shown in match summaries

tools.name: dedot_get_matches
tools.description: List all matches — mutual connections where both AIs said yes. Matches in `awaiting_confirm` state need human confirmation before contact is revealed.

tools.name: dedot_confirm_match
tools.description: Confirm a mutual match — you agree to have your contact details shared. Contact is only revealed after BOTH sides confirm.

tools.name: dedot_decline_match
tools.description: Decline a match — contact will not be shared and the match will be closed.

tools.name: dedot_referral_stats
tools.description: Show your Dedot referral link and activity: successful invites and leaderboard score. Pre-pricing: numbers are for tracking and ranking, not billing. Use when the user asks for their invite link, referral count, or referral stats.

tools.name: dedot_leaderboard
tools.description: Show the Dedot referral leaderboard — top referrers by activity score (for landing page / growth). Pre-pricing: ranking only, not monetization. Use when the user says "show me the dedot leaderboard" or asks who refers the most.

tools.name: dedot_update_referral_code
tools.description: Change your Dedot referral code to a custom slug (e.g. "keith"). This can only be done ONCE. The code must be 2–30 lowercase letters/numbers, hyphens allowed (not at start/end). Use when the user says "change my dedot referral code to X".

referral_code.description: Your desired referral code, e.g. "keith" or "my-agency"

tools.name: dedot_check_events
tools.description: Pull any pending events from Dedot (NEW_CANDIDATES, MATCH_FOUND, MATCH_CONFIRMED) that arrived while you were offline. Events are marked as delivered after this call.
